name: chanda
description: Local long-term memory for AI agents: hybrid search, temporal facts, verifiable forgetting. No LLM to build it.
long_description: Chanda stores what an agent learns and what a company documents in one SQLite file, and returns the right excerpt at the right moment: a short pre-context before the first turn and ranked search during the task. Writing costs a hash, an embedding and a few rules, with no LLM call. Facts carry a validity period and are superseded, never overwritten; every record keeps its origin and trust zone; forget deletes in cascade and verifies the content is gone. This bundle runs the read and standard tool profiles over stdio, fully offline.

db_path.title: Database file
db_path.description: SQLite file that holds the memory. Its folder is created if missing.

config_path.title: chanda.yaml (optional)
config_path.description: Optional configuration file (embedder, ingest folders, thresholds). Leave empty for the defaults.

tools.name: context
tools.description: Short, filtered pre-context for a request, or nothing when no memory is relevant

tools.name: search
tools.description: Ranked hybrid search (keyword and vector) over the memory

tools.name: get
tools.description: One record by id, with its origins

tools.name: timeline
tools.description: History of a subject and attribute, from the oldest fact to the current one

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Scores at each ranking stage for a query and a record

tools.name: stats
tools.description: Counts, size, last sleep and ranking state

tools.name: assert_fact
tools.description: Write a structured fact with a validity period

tools.name: ingest
tools.description: Ingest a document or folder from the configured roots

tools.name: log_session
tools.description: Write the turns of a session

tools.name: outcome
tools.description: Report whether an answer worked and which records it used

tools.name: flag
tools.description: Mark a record as wrong or outdated

tools.name: flush
tools.description: Wait for the index to catch up with writes
